channel.title: Module 5: The Graph Workflow Engine (core of ADK Go 2.x) on 梦兽编程
channel.description: Recent content in Module 5: The Graph Workflow Engine (core of ADK Go 2.x) on 梦兽编程

item.title: Dynamic graphs and HITL: RunNode's seven options, the adk_request_input wire format, and resuming across requests
item.description: The two hardest pieces of the ADK Go v2.6.0 graph engine together: runtime orchestration with DynamicNode + RunNode (the seven With* options, stable-RunID single-flight deduplication, failure classification, output delegation), the synthetic adk_request_input FunctionCall produced by NewRequestInputEvent and LongRunningToolIDs, the InterruptID uniqueness requirement (the Dev UI tracks answered requests by ID and never re-asks), the re-entry and handoff modes of RerunOnResume with the branch in duplicate-Resume semantics, the one-line ResumeOrRequestInput form, Workflow.Resume and ErrNothingToResume, how ReconstructRunState rebuilds state from event history (since v2.6.0 RunState is no longer persisted as a blob), and the hard limitation that parallel HITL is not supported.

item.title: Scheduler lifecycle and retries: seven node states, five backoffs, and a default that refuses to retry validation errors
item.description: The scheduling layer of the ADK Go v2.6.0 graph engine: the exact semantics of the seven NodeStatus values (including the two causes of NodeWaiting, why NodeRunning must be re-scheduled after a restart, and the two sources of NodeCancelled), the RunState event-history-rebuild model and binary-payload handling, DefaultRetryConfig's 5/1s/60s/2.0/full-jitter policy (since v2.6.0 the docs match the implementation: ErrInputValidation is not retried by default), the two exportable pure functions ShouldRetry and CalculateDelay, the struct literal versus DefaultRetryConfig trap, plus concurrency caps and cancellation propagation (cancelAll/echoesCancellation/nil on sibling cancellation).

item.title: Routing and conditional execution: what Default really means, silent dead ends, and a deduplicated edge
item.description: Conditional execution in ADK Go v2.6.0: how the Route interface reads event.Routes, the exact matching rules of StringRoute/IntRoute/BoolRoute/MultiRoute/Default, the four scheduling semantics in findSuccessors (unconditional edges do not suppress Default, Default fires only when no concrete route matched, all-miss-without-Default is a silent dead end, same-target deduplication), the per-activation hard constraints (ErrMultipleOutputs/ErrMultipleRoutingEvents/ErrMultipleTerminalOutputs), the implicit behaviour that a FunctionNode must return *session.Event to carry routes, branch derivation during fan-out, and the observable consequence of route-edge order becoming deterministic since v2.6.0 (byte-lexicographic).

item.title: Edges and the execution model: EdgeBuilder, the eight graph validations, and that single consumer goroutine
item.description: The wiring layer of the ADK Go v2.6.0 graph engine: Edge{From,To,Route} and the Start sentinel, EdgeBuilder's six methods plus Chain/Concat, the eight legality checks in workflow.New (duplicate edges, multiple default routes, unreachable nodes, unconditional cycles, sub-graph name collisions…), name being only a node-path prefix (a label, no longer a persistence namespace), AddRoutes' byte-lexicographic determinism, the one-goroutine-per-node plus single-consumer execution model, what yielding events in arrival order implies, and the userInput text concatenation rule.

item.title: All node types: the Node interface's eight methods, six built-in nodes, and NodeConfig's tri-state pointers
item.description: The node layer of the ADK Go v2.6.0 graph engine: when each of the eight workflow.Node methods is called, BaseNode and custom nodes, the four constructors of the FunctionNode family (including FromState's parameter binding and the node_input escape hatch), EmittingFunctionFn, the constructors and semantics of AgentNode/ToolNode/JoinNode/WorkflowNode/ParallelWorker (JoinNode's conditional-routing misconfiguration is called out in the v2.6.0 comment as unvalidated, silently skipped, with the run still reporting success), and why the six NodeConfig fields (ParallelWorker/RerunOnResume/WaitForOutput/RetryConfig/Timeout/EmitsOwnSpan) use pointers.
